name: National Taichung Theater
intro: A landmark performing-arts venue known for fluid 'sound cave' geometry.
history: Designed by Toyo Ito; opened 2016 as a new city icon in Taichung’s 7th Redevelopment Zone.

name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts
intro: Taiwan’s leading fine-arts museum with a campus layout and generous galleries.
history: Opened 1988; expanded with outdoor sculpture park along Calligraphy Greenway.

name: Taichung Railway Station (Old)
intro: Historic station building with red-brick facade and gables.
history: Completed 1917 during Japanese era; preserved after elevation project.

name: Taichung Railway Station (New Elevated Concourse)
structure: Steel frame and reinforced concrete decks
intro: Elevated station providing through-running rail with transparent concourse.
history: Part of TRA elevation program to remove level crossings and open ground space.

name: Miyahara (Former Ophthalmology Hospital)
intro: Adaptive reuse of a 1927 clinic into a dessert shop and library-like hall.
history: Restored after the 1999 quake; interior reimagined for retail and tourism.

name: Taichung Second Market
massing: Radial halls around a central hub
intro: Historic food market with spoke-like plan and narrow bays.
history: Established 1917; continues as a local culinary destination.

name: Taichung City Hall (Old Prefectural Hall)
intro: Former prefectural hall with classical composition and portico cues.
history: Japanese-era government building later used by Taichung City offices.

name: Taichung Broadcasting Bureau
intro: Historic radio building now used for culture and exhibitions.
history: Built in 1935; adaptive reuse for creative events.

name: Taichung Confucius Temple
intro: Confucian temple complex with axial symmetry and courtyards.
history: Built to serve education and rites; influenced by Song–Ming prototypes.

name: Taichung Martyrs’ Shrine
massing: Gate, court, main hall on axis
intro: Memorial complex on a stepped axis with ceremonial gate.
history: Converted from earlier Shinto site; used for official ceremonies.

name: Shenji New Village
intro: Former provincial staff housing turned creative market lanes.
history: Revitalized as cultural and small-business cluster.

name: Audit Village (Audit Office Dorms)
intro: Dormitory compound reused as studios and cafes near Calligraphy Greenway.
history: Government dorms transformed into a creative community.

name: Wufeng Lin Family Mansion and Garden
intro: Major historic residence with elaborate halls and gardens.
history: Seat of the Lin family; damaged in the 1999 quake and restored.

name: 921 Earthquake Museum of Taiwan
intro: Museum built around preserved quake-damaged school structures.
history: Adaptive reuse of Guangfu Junior High after the 1999 earthquake.

name: Luce Memorial Chapel (Tunghai University)
intro: Iconic chapel by I. M. Pei and Chi-kuan Chen with expressive shell form.
history: Completed 1963 on Tunghai campus; a key work of Taiwan modernism.

name: National Museum of Natural Science
intro: Large science museum with planetarium and botanical garden.
history: Opened 1986 and expanded over time.

name: Taichung HSR Station
intro: High-speed rail hub linking Taichung to the national corridor.
history: Opened 2006 with Taiwan High Speed Rail line.

name: Rainbow Village
intro: Veteran housing painted with vivid murals by 'Grandpa Rainbow'.
history: Grassroots preservation turned into a public art site.

name: Taichung Park Pavilion (Lake Pavilion)
intro: Historic lakeside pavilion in Taichung Park.
history: Japanese-era structure, a city symbol and leisure landmark.

name: Taichung City Seaport Art Center
intro: Coastal cultural venue serving the harbor area.
history: Built to promote arts in Taichung’s seaport district.

name: Taichung Mayoral Residence
intro: Elegant former mayor’s residence built under Japanese rule with Baroque-influenced ornament.
history: Declared a historic building in 2002; among the best preserved Western-style houses in Taichung.

name: Taichu Shiyakusho (Old Taichung City Office)
massing: Corner block winged by two arms
intro: 1911 Japanese-era municipal building now used as a café and art venue.
history: Renovated and reopened in 2016 as a cultural facility.

name: Shr-Hwa International Tower
intro: Skyscraper with a facade suggesting bamboo shoots.
history: Completed in 2004; tallest in Taichung for 14 years.

name: The Landmark (Taichung)
intro: Office tower, tallest in Taichung as of 2018; beige granite and grey glass exterior.
history: Completed 2018 in the 7th Redevelopment Zone.

name: National Trade Center (Taichung)
intro: Skyscraper designed to resemble a spring bamboo shoot symbolizing prosperity.
history: Completed 2018 as part of Taichung’s commercial core.

name: Fubon Sky Tree
intro: Residential tower by Toyo Ito with tree-like form and energy-saving facade.
history: Completed 2016.

name: Taichung Municipal Cultural Center
massing: Low slabs and heavy concrete forms
intro: Late-20th-century concrete institutional architecture in Taichung.
history: Still in use for cultural events and exhibitions.

name: Asia University Museum of Modern Art (Wufeng)
intro: Modern art museum on the Asia University campus with dramatic forms.
history: Designed as a campus landmark.

name: Dali Yi Museum (Former Meeting Hall)
massing: Single large hall with side wings
intro: Historic building originally a meeting hall, later a local museum.
history: Part of old Dali Yi street improvement; reused after the 1999 quake.

name: National Taichung University of Education
massing: Symmetrical main block with central pavilion and flanking wings
structure: Reinforced concrete frame with brick cladding
intro: Historic teacher-training campus in central Taichung with a landmark brick administration building fronting Minsheng Road.
history: Originated as Taichung Normal School in 1899; campus established at current site in the 1920s; evolved through several renamings to become National Taichung University of Education.

name: Taichung City Cultural Center / Taichung Gateway Park Complex
intro: Cultural-park complex providing large gathering spaces and shading in Taichung Gateway Park.
history: Competition-winning scheme; construction ongoing.

name: Yide Mansion (Yide New Village)
intro: Historic residence now revitalized for art and cafe uses.
history: Listed as a historic building in 2011.

name: Wanchungong (Wan-Chung Temple)
massing: Single central hall with side wings
intro: Historic Matsu temple in Taichung’s old city.
history: Among the oldest religious sites in Taichung, repeatedly restored.

name: Fengyuan Railway Station (New)
intro: Station from the railway elevation project in Fengyuan.
history: Part of revitalized old-town transportation infrastructure.

name: CMP Block Museum of Arts (Outdoor)
intro: Private outdoor art park connecting to Calligraphy Greenway with rotating installations.
history: Developed to activate the Greenway cultural spine.

name: Taichung Park (Park Landscapes)
intro: Large public park in the city center with historic elements.
history: Opened 1903; still a major leisure venue.

name: Green Museumbrary (Art Museum + Public Library)
intro: New cultural landmark by SANAA combining an art museum and public library.
history: Phased opening from December 2025.

name: Taichung City Office Building (Historic)
intro: Historic municipal building noted in Taichung architecture surveys.
history: Built during the Japanese era; retains civic heritage value.

name: Maple Garden (Qiuhonggu Park) Pavilion & Bridge
massing: Sunken lake with perimeter paths and bridges
intro: Iconic sunken park with reflective lake and pedestrian bridges in the 7th Redevelopment Zone.
history: Created to introduce green relief within a high-density district.

name: Taichung First Square (Market Mall)
intro: Large indoor market-mall known for migrant community shops and food courts.
history: Evolved from a traditional market into a vertical bazaar.

name: Taichung Marathon Cultural Centre
massing: Long linear building with full glass facade
intro: Venue for large cultural and sports events in the redevelopment zone.
history: Added to city infrastructure during the 2010s.

name: Fulfillment Amphitheater (Wenxin Forest Park)
intro: Major outdoor performance venue set in a forest park.
history: Built to host city festivals and concerts.

name: Taichung Literature Museum
massing: One- to two-storey compound around courtyards
intro: Historic dorms adapted into a literature museum with small gardens and verandas.
history: Preserved and adapted to showcase Taichung’s literary heritage.

name: Rainbow Village (Site)
intro: Housing estate repainted into a vibrant art destination.
history: Re-imagined as a public art site and tourist draw.

name: Taichung City Hall (New)
intro: Modern city administration building serving the 7th Redevelopment Zone.
history: Built as part of westward expansion of the civic core.

name: Huludun Cultural Center
massing: Low wings around a central hall
intro: District-level arts venue with galleries, library services, and community programs.
history: Expanded and renovated to support northern Taichung’s cultural needs.

name: Luce Memorial Chapel (Shell)
intro: Iconic chapel on Tunghai University campus by I. M. Pei and Chen Chi-kuan.
history: Completed 1963; modernist landmark in Taiwan.

name: Shuinan Central Park Visitor Center
intro: Gateway pavilion for Taichung Central Park with orientation, exhibits, and shade.
history: Part of the Shuinan aerotropolis regeneration.

name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts – Expansion Pavilion
intro: Major expansion of Taiwan’s leading fine-arts museum campus.
history: Opened circa 2019–2020 to grow the institution’s footprint.

name: Wufeng Lin Family Mansion and Garden – East Wing Restoration
intro: Large historic residence turned museum complex.
history: Seat of the Lin family; restored after the 1999 quake.

name: Taichung Municipal Library – West Branch
massing: Low horizontal volume with open plaza
intro: Modern library branch providing open and transparent space.
history: Part of the city’s library network revitalization.

name: Tunghai University Administrative Building
intro: Administrative building on Tunghai campus with modernist simplicity and landscape integration.
history: Built in the early years of the university.

name: Fengchia Night Market Urban Edge Building
intro: Tower adjacent to a major night-market zone, part of urban intensification.
history: Built as part of redevelopment near Feng Chia University.

name: Taichung Science Park R&D Centre
massing: Low horizontal blocks with research towers
intro: Building complex supporting Taiwan’s science industry in Taichung’s Science Park.
history: Part of an economic development zone.

name: Taichung International Airport Terminal (Older Section)
massing: Low flat-roof terminal with jet bridges
intro: Original terminal building before expansions; important civic transport node.
history: Older section predates recent expansions; served domestic and some international traffic.

name: Calligraphy Greenway Corridor Buildings
intro: Mixed-use buildings along a cultural corridor linking museums and parks.
history: Developed as part of the city’s cultural renewal.

name: Taichung Veterans General Hospital Branch
intro: Hospital building from the 1970s with solid concrete architecture.
history: Expanded repeatedly; remains a major medical facility.

name: Blue Focus Creative Hub (Adapted Warehouse)
massing: Low rectangular building with large openings
intro: Former industrial warehouse converted to creative offices and galleries.
history: Part of neighborhood revitalization.

name: Taichung High Court / Former Magistrate’s Office
intro: Historical court building now a heritage museum and legal center.
history: Built under Japanese rule, preserved as a historic site.

name: Taichung Fine Arts Park Pavilion (Outdoor Art Building)
intro: Glass pavilion for outdoor art exhibitions within the fine-arts park.
history: Built to expand the museum campus publicly.

name: Xinshe Castle (Shin-She Castle)
intro: Tourist-themed castle complex in the Xinshe hills; a popular photo spot.
history: Built to attract leisure tourism.
